name: Trypan Blue Cell Viability Calculator
seoTitle: Trypan Blue Cell Viability Calculator — Formula & Results
seoDesc: Trypan blue viability is live cells divided by live plus dead cells, as a percentage. Free trypan blue cell viability calculator: enter your values and get vi
summary:
Trypan blue viability is live cells divided by live plus dead cells, as a percentage. It returns viability, live cell concentration and live cells in 10 mL, and the panel shows all of them at once.

The same count, corrected for the squares counted and the dilution, gives the live cell concentration and the live cells in a fixed volume. Press Calculate and the results appear in the grey boxes; after the first press they keep up with every edit, so there is no page to reload. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the Trypan Blue Cell Viability
sections.html:
Viability (%) = live ÷ (live + dead) × 100; live cells/mL = (live ÷ squares) × dilution × 10⁴

The symbols in the formula
SymbolWhat it stands forUnit
liveunstained, refractile cellscells
deadblue-stained cellscells
dilutiontotal dilution including the dye×

sections.title: How do I use the Trypan Blue Cell Viability?
sections.html:
Every input sits in the same order the formula is written, so the page reads like the equation.

  1. Enter the values you already have. Every box accepts a decimal point and a minus sign; thousands separators are ignored.
  2. The grey boxes are results: they are worked out from your inputs and cannot be typed into.
  3. Press Calculate. The results fill in together, and from then on they follow every edit you make — there is no page to reload and nothing to submit.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: live cells counted of 280 cells, dead cells counted of 40 cells, squares counted of 4, dilution factor of 2 ×.

Substituting them into the formula gives viability of 87.5%, live cell concentration of 1,400,000 cells/mL, live cells in 10 ml of 14,000,000 cells.

Those numbers come from the same solver the page runs in your browser, not from an illustration, so typing different inputs moves the answer exactly as the arithmetic says.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
The number on its own is not a judgement. These are the bands most often used when the result is quoted in a paper, a report or a label:

How to read the result
ResultBandWhat it means
above 95%Healthytypical of a log-phase culture
85 – 95%Acceptablefine for most assays
below 85%Poorcheck handling, medium and time since harvest

  • Count within five minutes of adding the dye: longer and live cells start taking it up.

  • Viability by dye exclusion overestimates health — a stressed cell that still excludes dye counts as live. Pair it with growth or an ATP assay for anything critical.

  • Report live-cell density, not total, whenever you seed a plate: dead cells do not divide.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
These are the errors that account for almost every wrong answer people bring to this calculator:

  • Forgetting the dye dilution in the concentration calculation.
  • Counting too few cells, which makes the percentage jump by several points per cell.
  • Leaving the haemocytometer to dry between samples, which concentrates the cells.

faq.q: Why do my live cells look blue?
faq.a: They have been in the dye too long, or the suspension is acidic. Recount within five minutes.

faq.q: Is trypan blue toxic to cells?
faq.a: It is excluded by intact membranes but is cytotoxic over time, so count before plating.

faq.q: What does the Trypan Blue Cell Viability actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns viability, live cell concentration and live cells in 10 mL. Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.

faq.q: Can I use it with the numbers straight from a datasheet?
faq.a: Yes. Every box states its unit, and nothing is converted behind your back, so a figure copied from a datasheet, a kit insert or a protocol goes in as printed.
